Features of Instagram reels

Plot 1

## Plot 1 - Decription

The plot is based on Instagram reels and comparing the number of reels that do or do not contain a soundtrack, where there are different reels across a period of 2/3 months (March, April, May). Various methods were used to help achieve this plot, and the reason why I wanted to see if there was a difference of the reels that appeared on my Instagram feed when I completed Project 2 in March/April compared to when I was completing Project 4.

From the plot, the difference between the reels that had a soundtrack vs those that had a soundtrack at the time of Project 2 is mostly similar to the difference between the reels that had a soundtrack vs those that had a soundtrack of when Project 4 was being completed. This was quite interesting because I expected that reels that contained a soundtrack would have a higher proportion, as I felt that reels that have music receive more views, thus resulting in a higher likelihood of appearing on users’ Instagram feeds.

Plot 2

## Plot 2 - Decription

I decided to create a box plot, comparing the number of posts made by the Instagram accounts that had their reels appear on my Instagram feed, and the number of followers (accounts that had over a million followers vs accounts that had under a million followers). I was interested to see if accounts that had a higher number of posts had more than a million followers, but when looking at the plot that’s not the case in this scenario. From the plot, the IQR of the accounts that had less than a million followers is greater than the IQR of the accounts that had more than a million followers, which is quite surprising.

Another thing to note is that the median number of posts between the groups isn’t too far. I filtered the data by only keeping reels that had over 500 posts and less than and equal to 3500 posts, and the reason I did this was because when I looked at the data, I saw that there were reels that had a very low number of posts and reels that had a extremely high number of posts, and I didn’t want that to affect the result of the plot in a significant way. While the output of the plot was surprising, the result could’ve been affected by a difference in proportion (e.g. there could’ve been more reels that had less than a million followers compared to reels that had more than a million followers).

Plot 3

## Plot 3 - Decription

In this plot, the comparison between the number of posts made by Instagram accounts vs the period of when the reels had appeared on my Instagram feed is made through a dot plot. When looking at the plot, most of the dots are scattered in one area, with a few outliers being present. However, there seems to be more of a variation in the reels that had appeared during May. This could be an indication of different content creators with various levels of popularity getting more recognition, as more reels have been created since March/April. The mean number of posts is slightly higher for reels that had appeared on people’s Instagram feed in May compared to the mean number of posts for reels that had appeared on people’s Instagram feed in March/April. This plot also shows how having an extremely high number of posts isn’t necessary for a reel to appear on an Instagram feed.
